newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end weaker, small issues shine.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end weaker, small issues shine.

text.p: Singapore shares ended weaker in listless trade on Thursday with punters turning to smaller capitalisation stocks as blue chips were side-stepped.
Dealers said retail players accumulated new issues, focusing on a handful of U.S-dollar stocks, while institutions shunned Singapore companies with exposure to Thailand.

"The reaction on Thailand's floation of the baht should in the longer term make people nervous," a Singapore bank dealer said. He added that the spurt in Malaysian over-the-counter stocks on Wednesday in reaction to bullish Thai stocks was speculative and could not be sustained.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) fell 6.51 points to 1,962.40. The UOB OTC index of Malaysian stocks also fell, by 8.09 points to 1,138.09.
Volume was a mere 126 million lots with losers beating gainers 204 to 134 contracts.
Dealers said the volatile Hong Kong stock market, re-opening on the first day of trade under Chinese rule, also stifled activity on the Singapore bourse.
The dollar's strength in Asia helped support some issues.
Cable and telecommunications manufacturer Huan Hsin hit a high of US$0.545, and ended up $0.005 at $0.52.
Electronics firm Lung Kee Metal rose to close at a new high of US$1.27, up seven cents.
Top of the actives was Tye Soon which ended at S$0.56, up four cents on turnover of 13.3 million shares.
Raffles Medical Group also peaked at a high of S$1.12, and ended at S$1.10, up six cents on takeover talks.
Major components of the STI index dragged it lower. Cycle & Carriage, fell 40 cents to S$14.40, and Cerebos Pacific, eased 25 cents at S$5.85.
